output:
Dear Larkspur Lofts Residents,

I’m writing to address concerns about the drone I flew from the roof deck on Saturday, October 31, around 4 p.m. I live in unit 5A and have been a resident here for three years. I want to explain what I was doing, acknowledge the concern it caused, and outline how I will handle this going forward.

I’m a wedding photographer, and I was testing a new Halvard Mini 4 drone before photographing a vineyard wedding in Dundee. The flight lasted approximately 11 minutes. Throughout that time, the camera was pointed west toward the river and the Fremont Bridge, not toward anyone’s windows. I was not using it to observe residents or their homes.

Even so, I understand that a drone hovering over the courtyard could feel intrusive or unsettling without that context. I’m sorry my flight worried people. I should have considered how it would look and sound to neighbors rather than assuming its purpose would be clear.

Anyone who would like to see the full, unedited footage is welcome to knock on my door at 5A or email me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example. I’m happy to show it and answer questions.

Our current HOA rules do not address drones, but I recognize that this leaves an issue we should resolve together. I will ask the board to add it to the agenda for the November 19 meeting at 7 p.m. in the community room. I will not fly from the roof again until the board decides on a rule.

I also want to respectfully address the lobby note. Posting my unit number alongside an accusation of spying and a personal insult was hurtful and not an appropriate way to raise a concern. Residents should be able to voice privacy concerns without anyone being publicly singled out or insulted.

If something I do causes concern in the future, please speak with me directly or email me so we can address it respectfully. I value living here and want our shared spaces to feel comfortable for everyone.

Sincerely,  
Jess Okafor  
Unit 5A
